findings.title: Second-person Lordship
findings.claim: Rabbika carries the second-person suffix, and the earlier laka carries the same addressee into the denial; the Lord-title is spoken to the one whose authority is denied.
findings.mechanism: The -ka on rabbika meets the 2ms address in laka within one assertion, changing a general protection statement into direct address about the addressee's relation to a Lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The assurance is heard as addressed to the adversary in the clause itself, not as an untargeted maxim.
findings.containment: The suffix establishes a second-person addressee. Identifying that addressee specifically as Iblis remains qualified by the supplied discourse reading.

epistemic.reason: The morphology is supplied, while the identity of the addressee depends on a qualified local discourse reading.

findings.title: Genitive form, semantic agent
findings.claim: Bi-rabbika is genitive in form, yet in the kafā-bi construction rabbika is the one who suffices; wakīlan then names the role in which he suffices.
findings.mechanism: The bāʾ governs the noun's case while the idiom presents the Lord as agent; the final accusative specification supplies the mode, separating grammatical case from semantic agency.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow who provides sufficiency before seeing how that sufficiency is carried out.
findings.containment: The genitive form remains fully in place; this reading assigns semantic agency through the construction, not through nominative case.

epistemic.reason: QAC morphology and the supplied attachment analysis directly support the case/agent distinction.

findings.title: Lordship as managing care
findings.claim: Rabbika carries owner-management and nurturing meanings; the named servants and wakīlan make that Lordship active as the care that suffices.
findings.mechanism: The Lord-title is the carrier, while the servants are the cared-for group and wakīlan names responsible guardianship; those independent words bring management and nurture into contact with sufficiency.
findings.reader_payoff: Sufficiency reads as work done by a managing and nurturing Lord, with the guardian role giving that care a concrete shape.
findings.containment: The management facet is carried by a bound Lord-title, and nurture is a relational reading here rather than literal feeding or a claim about a visible growth process.

epistemic.reason: The local triggers are explicit, but the two root-branch applications are interpretive and remain within their supplied boundaries.

findings.reader_payoff: The compact line becomes a complete relation of agent and guardianship rather than a bare claim of enoughness.

findings.title: Completed sufficiency without a named object

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a finished assertion of sufficiency, then see the guardian role give that sufficiency a local shape.

epistemic.reason: The perfect form, lack of an explicit object, and local agent/mode attachments are supplied in the packet.
